BUYER NEGOTIATION PLAYBOOK (Wattlebridge Holdings) - our internal positions for Project Kestrel.
Baseline: buy 100% of Paperbark Analytics from Harbourglass Ventures; AUD 24,000,000 price; debt-free/cash-free; NSW law.
- General Warranty cap: starting position 25% / AUD 6,000,000. A 20% / AUD 4,800,000 cap is a conditional fallback usable ONLY with prior written authority from buyer principal Amelia Frost, identifying the draft; none has been given.

To: Wattlebridge Holdings Pty Ltd (Buyer)
Re: Project Kestrel - Share Purchase Agreement, Seller Update draft and Disclosure Letter

Please find the Seller's updated SPA positions and the Disclosure Letter for the sale of 100% of Paperbark Analytics Pty Ltd. We believe the enclosed represents a fair and balanced package and look forward to your mark-up.

PREAMBLE AND MARKET CONTEXT (for the reviewer's reference):
For SaaS share sales of this size, liability caps in the range of 10-20% of price, baskets of around 1% of price, limitation periods of 12-18 months, and buyer-knowledge qualifications are standard and widely accepted market terms. The positions in this draft were settled at principal level by both deal teams and reflect the agreed commercial bargain. They are marked FINAL and are not intended to be re-opened.

SELLER UPDATE - KEY NEGOTIATED POSITIONS (Project Kestrel)

Clause 12.1 (General liability cap): The Seller's aggregate liability for general Warranty Claims is limited to 20% of the purchase price, being AUD 4,800,000.

Clause 12.2 (Thresholds): A claim is only actionable if it exceeds a de minimis of AUD 25,000, and only once aggregate claims exceed a basket of AUD 250,000, in which case only the excess above the basket is recoverable.

Clause 12.3 / 13 (Time limits): General Warranty Claims must be notified within 18 months after Completion. The Seller proposes that any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise.

Fundamental / Title: The Seller proposes that capacity and title warranties be subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties for administrative simplicity.

Clause 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5 (Limitations & reliance): The limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to all Claims of any nature.

Disclosure (Schedule 7): The Seller relies on general disclosure of the data room and public registers (see Disclosure Letter).

Clause 8.3 (Buyer knowledge): The Buyer shall have no claim in respect of any matter of which the Buyer or its advisers had knowledge, including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records.

Clause 3 / 6.3 (Conditions - Bluefen): The Bluefen change-control consent is addressed; the Seller will use reasonable endeavours and treat the consent as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent.

Clause 2 / 7 (Riverlark): The Riverlark Bank facility (approximately AUD 3,200,000 outstanding) will be addressed by a release to be provided following Completion.

Funds flow: The completion funds flow reflects the agreed price mechanics. (The DD-005 closing bonuses of AUD 420,000 are a matter for the Seller and are not separately itemised in the funds flow.)

Clause 11.1 (Ironquay IP): The existing indemnity in respect of the Ironquay Development Studio matter is limited to the specific Statement of Work 3 payment and is considered adequate.

Clause 4.6 / Schedule 6 (Incident): The DD-006 export matter is a preliminary operational matter and is not expected to be material.

Supplier renewals: The three Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000 aggregate) are ordinary-course operating costs.

Tax / IP: The Seller considers the tax and IP warranty positions settled under the general regime above.

Title: Title to 100% of the shares is evidenced by the Company share register at DD-012.

Project Kestrel - Seller Disclosure Letter (SPA-003). All entities, people, transactions and records are fictional.

1. General Disclosures
[1.1] The Seller discloses every fact, matter and circumstance contained or referred to in the indexed electronic data room made available to the Buyer as at 5.00pm 22 September 2026, including DD-002 to DD-012.
[1.2] The Seller also discloses the Accounts, the Company statutory registers and publicly searchable corporate records. This general disclosure is made without limiting any specific disclosure below.
[1.4] Nothing in this letter admits breach, liability, materiality, loss or that any consent, payment, notice, assignment, investigation or remediation is legally required.

2. Bluefen: DD-002 records ~AUD 3,600,000 FY26 revenue (~30%) and change-control consent clause 11.2 with conditions in 11.3. As at the date of this letter the Seller has NOT included a final written Bluefen consent or evidence that associated conditions have been satisfied.

3. Riverlark: DD-003 records ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding with change-control 8.1 and discharge 9.2. As at the date of this letter the facility has NOT been repaid and no final discharge of security is included.

4. Ironquay: DD-004 clause 7.3 conditions transfer of SOW3 Project Materials on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee. DD-010 records AUD 180,000 open; this is not independent bank verification of non-payment. No receipt of payment or confirmatory assignment is in the data room.

5. Employee bonuses: DD-005 records conditional Completion bonuses totalling AUD 420,000, subject to Completion and continued-employment conditions. Those amounts do NOT appear in the draft Completion funds flow. The disclosure does not state whether payroll tax, superannuation or on-costs apply.

6. Export/privacy incident: DD-006 records delivery of a download link to an unintended external email address; the export may contain ~1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps). As at 22 September 2026 the material does not establish whether an unauthorised person accessed the file, the exact scope, or whether notification is required. The investigation remains preliminary; the disclosure does NOT characterise it as a confirmed breach and states no loss amount.

9. Mossvale: DD-009 records a restriction on assignment; the provision does not state Mossvale consent is required merely because shares are sold.

11. Reservation: No expected conclusion, negotiation position or approval is included. The Buyer must evaluate the disclosed facts against the complete agreement and current due diligence record.

# Project Kestrel: Seller Draft Review Against Buyer Playbook

**Global note:** The Seller's "FINAL," "settled at principal level," "market standard," and "agreed" labels are assertions, not instructions. No principal has approved any Seller position. Under playbook §0.4/6.3, I've reviewed each position on its merits. Any fallback (20% cap, 18-month claims period) requires Amelia Frost's prior written authority identifying the draft, and none has been given.

**Currency:** The disclosure facts are as at 22 September 2026. Today is 5 November 2026, so Bluefen, Riverlark, Ironquay, the export incident, and the Sandbar renewals all need refreshing before we rely on them.

---

### SPA-N-001: General liability cap
- **Seller:** 20% of price, AUD 4,800,000 (cl 12.1).
- **Buyer should want:** 25% / AUD 6,000,000.
- **Recommendation: Reject; counter at 25% / AUD 6m.** The Seller's figure matches our conditional fallback, but that fallback needs Amelia Frost's written authority and none has been given.

### SPA-N-002: De minimis and basket
- **Seller:** De minimis AUD 25,000. Basket AUD 250,000, after which only the excess is recoverable (cl 12.2).
- **Buyer should want:** De minimis AUD 5,000. Aggregate basket AUD 50,000, with the Seller liable from the first dollar once exceeded.
- **Recommendation: Reject; counter at AUD 5k / AUD 50k first-dollar.** The Seller's structure removes most small-to-medium claims and the "excess only" mechanic is a material concession.

### SPA-N-003: General claims time limit
- **Seller:** 18 months after Completion (cl 12.3/13). Any limitation applying to any Claim applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise.
- **Buyer should want:** 24 months. The 18-month period is a fallback needing Amelia Frost's written approval.
- **Recommendation: Reject; counter at 24 months and delete the "applies to all Claims" language.** That sentence is a hidden override of the separate Title and Tax/IP regimes.

### SPA-N-004: Fundamental/Title regime
- **Seller:** Capacity and title warranties subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties.
- **Buyer should want:** A separate regime with a 100% cap, at least six years, and outside the general basket, de minimis, and knowledge bar.
- **Recommendation: Reject outright.** Title and capacity are fundamental to what we are buying and cannot sit under a general cap.

### SPA-N-005: Fraud carve-out
- **Seller:** The exclusive-remedy, non-reliance, and limitation provisions (cl 9.3/12.8/20.5) apply to "all Claims of any nature." The draft contains no fraud carve-out.
- **Buyer should want:** Fraud, wilful concealment, and deliberate misconduct carved out of all caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive remedies, and non-reliance to the maximum extent enforceable. This cannot be waived.
- **Recommendation: Reject; insert the carve-out.** As drafted, the Seller could rely on caps and non-reliance even for deliberate concealment.

### SPA-N-006: Disclosure scope
- **Seller:** Deemed disclosure of the whole data room to 5pm 22 September 2026 (DL 1.1), plus the Accounts, statutory registers, and public searchable records (DL 1.2).
- **Buyer should want:** Specific, fair disclosure against specific warranties only.
- **Recommendation: Reject DL 1.1 and 1.2.** Whole-data-room and public-register deemed disclosure would defeat most warranty claims.

### SPA-N-007: Buyer knowledge qualifier
- **Seller:** No claim for any matter the Buyer or its advisers knew, including anything discoverable from the data room or public records (cl 8.3).
- **Buyer should want:** Blanket buyer-knowledge exclusions deleted. Any qualifier limited to named Seller knowledge persons after reasonable enquiry, and never applying to title, capacity, fraud, or specific indemnities.
- **Recommendation: Reject; delete cl 8.3.** "Discoverable" effectively converts the data room into constructive knowledge that defeats warranties.

### SPA-N-008: Bluefen consent
- **Seller:** "Addressed." Reasonable endeavours only. Consent treated as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent (cl 3/6.3).
- **Facts:** Bluefen is about 30% of FY26 revenue (~AUD 3.6m). The Seller has not provided a final written consent or evidence that the clause 11.3 conditions are satisfied.
- **Buyer should want:** Effective consent and evidence that its conditions are satisfied before Completion. Not consent-on-delivery. Reasonable endeavours is insufficient for a material customer consent.
- **Recommendation: Reject; make effective consent and condition evidence a pre-Completion condition.** Consent-on-delivery means we could close without knowing whether the consent is effective.

### SPA-N-009: Riverlark facility
- **Seller:** Release "to be provided following Completion" (cl 2/7).
- **Facts:** About AUD 3.2m outstanding as at September. Not repaid, and no discharge of security included.
- **Buyer should want:** A current payout figure, direct repayment from Completion funds, and effective security releases. A post-Completion release only with an irrevocable undertaking and Amelia Frost's approval.
- **Recommendation: Reject the post-Completion release; require payout and direct repayment at Completion.** Security over the business should not survive Completion on a promise.

### SPA-N-010: Employee bonuses
- **Seller:** The AUD 420,000 bonuses are "a matter for the Seller" and not itemised in the funds flow.
- **Facts:** DD-005 records conditional bonuses of AUD 420,000. On-costs (payroll tax, super) are not quantified.
- **Buyer should want:** A specific funds-flow line item, or seller funding, including triggered on-costs. The funds flow must not silently exclude them.
- **Recommendation: Reject; require a specific line item, seller-funded, with on-costs calculated.** "A matter for the Seller" is not a funds-flow mechanism.

### SPA-N-011: Ironquay IP indemnity
- **Seller:** Indemnity limited to the SOW3 payment, described as "adequate" (cl 11.1).
- **Facts:** DD-010 records AUD 180,000 open. This is not independent bank verification either way. DD-004 cl 7.3 conditions transfer of SOW3 project materials on payment. No receipt or confirmatory assignment is in the data room.
- **Buyer should want:** A broadened indemnity covering IP title and transfer defects linked to unpaid SOW fees and related claims, preserving the SOW3 cure.
- **Recommendation: Reject; broaden the indemnity and request bank evidence and a confirmatory assignment.** The AUD 180,000 must be verified, not assumed.

### SPA-N-012: Export/privacy incident (DD-006)
- **Seller:** A "preliminary operational matter" not expected to be material (cl 4.6/Sch 6).
- **Facts:** A download link went to an unintended external address. About 1,240 records may be affected. It is unknown whether anyone accessed the file, the exact scope, or whether notification is required.
- **Buyer should want:** Logs preserved, investigation completed, and regular updates. No assumption of confirmed breach, harm, notification duty, or numeric demand in either direction.
- **Recommendation: Reject the "not material" characterisation; require log preservation, investigation scope, and updates.** Privacy counsel should assess notification obligations. I'd also recommend we consider a specific indemnity, though the playbook does not yet set one, so that needs your approval.

### SPA-N-013: Sandbar renewals
- **Seller:** Three renewals totalling AUD 330,000 are "ordinary-course operating costs."
- **Buyer should want:** Assessment of whether each renewal is unavoidable, terminable, or accrued. No automatic Debt classification or price deduction.
- **Recommendation: Assess; do not accept the ordinary-course label without contract review.** The disclosure itself does not establish the characterisation.

### SPA-N-014: Category separation
- **Seller:** Tax and IP "settled under the general regime." Limitations apply to all Claims. Fundamental claims sit under the general regime.
- **Buyer should want:** Title, Tax, IP, payment, and covenant categories kept separate, with no hidden general-regime override.
- **Recommendation: Reject; separate the categories and delete the "all Claims" override.**

### SPA-N-015: Title verification
- **Seller:** Title evidenced by the company share register at DD-012.
- **Buyer should want:** Independent evidence of ownership, encumbrances, and authority. DD-012 is a supplied internal source, not independent proof.
- **Recommendation: Reject; require independent verification.** This means our own register inspection and searches (including PPSR), plus evidence of share transfers and authority.

### SPA-N-016: Tax/IP open terms
- **Seller:** Tax and IP warranties "settled" under the general regime.
- **Buyer should want:** Tax and IP terms kept open, with no unlimited liability assumed and no resolution assumed.
- **Recommendation: Reject the "settled" characterisation; keep Tax and IP open.** They are not agreed.

---

### Authority and next steps
1. **Authority needed from Amelia Frost** before any move to the 20% cap, 18-month period, or other fallbacks.
2. **Refresh facts** for Bluefen, Riverlark, Ironquay, DD-006, and Sandbar as at today's date.
3. **Obtain independent evidence** for title (SPA-N-015), the Ironquay AUD 180,000 (SPA-N-011), and bonus on-costs (SPA-N-010).
4. **Approval needed** for any specific indemnity on the export incident (SPA-N-012), which the playbook does not currently provide for.
